description: Multiple-entry student visas were permitted for Iranians from 2010, but only for students of the social sciences. Students in technical and engineering fields are not eligible and receive single-entry visas only.
energy_note: Your field of study decides whether you may ever go home.
notes: FOUND ONLY IN PERSIAN SOURCES. Not surfaced by English-language search. Worth confirming against a State Department reciprocity schedule, which is where visa validity and entries are actually published.

aspect: EXAMPLE - you are not told which you qualify for
description: Iranian applicants are not told whether they are eligible for a multiple-entry visa. To find out, they must risk the visa they hold, leave the United States, and reapply - discovering the answer only at that point.
money_note: A trip abroad plus a fresh application to learn your own status.
time_note: And a new administrative processing hold if the answer is no.
energy_note: The only way to learn the rule is to gamble everything on it.

description: Single entry plus a Visas Mantis hold on re-application means a technical student who leaves for a funeral may not get back for a year, or at all. This is the mechanism behind the 'stop leaving' behaviour in SEC-003.

Persian coverage of the 2025 restrictions lists the exempt groups: green card holders, dual nationals travelling on a non-designated passport, Olympic and World Cup athletes, US government employees, people with proven family ties, and those holding a valid visa issued before the rule took effect.

aspect: EXAMPLE - what Persian-language guidance tells applicants to do
description: The practical advice given in Persian is the same as the English: during administrative processing nothing can be done unless the consulate requests something, in which case answer fast and completely. Otherwise, follow the case and wait.
energy_note: The advice, in every language, is to wait.

aspect: SCENARIO - the funeral he does not attend
description: Omid is a mechanical engineering PhD student in Michigan on a single-entry F-1. His grandmother dies in Isfahan. If he flies home he must reapply in Yerevan, and the last three people in his lab who did that waited eight, eleven and nineteen months. He watches the burial on a video call at 3am and goes to a seminar at nine.
energy_note: The single most common sentence in this whole dataset: he did not go.
